en.title: 10 Games From 2026 You Should Absolutely Skip
en.summary: While 2026 was a banner year for gaming, not every title hit the mark. We've sifted through the duds to highlight the ten worst games you're better off avoiding.
en.body:
## 1. Sonic Frontiers: Definitive Edition (Switch 2)
While the original Sonic Frontiers was a step in a new direction for the Blue Blur, this Switch 2 "Definitive Edition" is a baffling misstep. Despite the new console's power, it suffers from persistent pop-in, poor image quality, and even longer loading times than the original Switch version, making it a disappointing port for owners of the previous iteration.

## 2. The 9th Charnel
Promising a "rich, narrative experience" through a vague Steam description, The 9th Charnel fails to deliver on its scant promises. With six playable characters and an unclear premise, this title quickly devolves into a confusing and unengaging experience that leaves players lost rather than invested.

## 3. Code Violet
Team Kill Media's Code Violet is a prime example of a game that falters on almost every level. Criticized for its abysmal presentation, flat characters, nonsensical story, and fundamentally broken gameplay, it's further plagued by significant technical issues that make it almost unplayable.

## 4. Star Wars Eclipse
Despite considerable hype, Star Wars Eclipse landed with a thud due to significant development issues and a lackluster final product. Reports of questionable balancing, frustrating matchmaking, and a general failure to capture the Star Wars magic meant this ambitious title struggled to gain any traction with players.

## 5. High on Life 2
While Game Informer lauded High on Life 2 with top scores, player reception was far more divided. Many found the sequel to be a tedious slog, failing to recapture the initial charm or innovative gameplay that made the first installment a hit, leading to a disappointing experience for many.

## 6. LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight
Although praised by some outlets, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight proved to be a surprisingly underwhelming entry in the beloved LEGO series. The game struggled with repetitive gameplay loops and a lack of innovation, failing to offer the fresh, engaging experience fans have come to expect from TT Games.

## 7. Denshattack
This title, which received high marks from some reviewers, failed to impress a broader audience. Denshattack's niche appeal and perhaps overly complex mechanics meant it struggled to find its footing, leaving many players bewildered rather than entertained by its unique premise.

## 8. Bioware's Latest RPG
While Bioware is known for its narrative prowess, their latest RPG offering in 2026 received mixed reactions. Players reported issues ranging from clunky combat to a story that didn't quite land, leaving fans hoping for a return to form in future projects.

## 9. Armored Core 6
FromSoftware's Armored Core 6, while technically impressive, proved to be a divisive title. Many found the steep learning curve and complex customization overwhelming, while others felt the core gameplay loop became repetitive, preventing it from achieving universal acclaim.

## 10. OCTOPATH TRAVELER (Sequel/New Entry)
Following up on a beloved predecessor is never easy, and the latest OCTOPATH TRAVELER title in 2026 was no exception. While visually stunning, many players felt the narrative structure and character interactions didn't evolve significantly, leading to a sense of déjà vu rather than a fresh adventure.
Bottom Line: With so many incredible games released in 2026, these ten serve as stark reminders that even the best years have their share of avoidable disappointments.

content_raw: 2 026 will go down as one of the best years in gaming, and that’s without even counting Grand Theft Auto 6 . However, for every gem, hidden or otherwise, that deserves your attention, hundreds of other titles exist that aren’t worth the trouble. And among that bunch are some truly abysmal offerings that serve as little more than black holes for your time, energy and faith in gaming. So naturally, we’ve scanned that dreg heap to pick the ten worst games of the year in no particular order. Let’s start with perhaps the most surprising of the bunch… Sonic Frontiers: Definitive Edition (Switch 2) “Hold on,” you’re doubtless typing upon seeing this, probably followed shortly after by “How dare you” and “If you bring up Sonic ’06 , so help me.” And honestly, that reaction is justified. When Sonic Frontiers launched in 2022, it signaled a new beginning for everyone’s favorite Blue Blur, selling millions of copies despite some good but not spectacular reviews. Sonic Team continued supporting it with new content, ending on a mostly high note with The Final Horizon. So what’s the problem with the Definitive Edition ? Well, it’s actually the Nintendo Switch 2 version, and despite the console’s increased power, it’s barely improved over the Switch 1 release. It runs better, sure, but still suffers from some pretty terrible pop-in and poor image quality. Loading times are somehow longer than on the Switch 1 and, worst of all, original owners can’t upgrade…which feels pointless anyway since all the included content is free. Sonic Frontiers: Definitive Edition doesn’t sink to the level of the franchise’s worst entries, but the disservice that the developer has done to it with this port is all the more damning. The 9th Charnel A Steam description that doesn’t really tell you what the game is about while promising a “rich, narrative experience”? Six playable characters with their own “unique backstory and motivations”? So-called “realistic graphics” despite every screenshot indicating otherwise? The 9th Charne l may as well be playing Minesweeper with all these red flags. Between the sheer number of AI problems, the lack of polish, the awful cutscenes, how terrible it feels to control, and so much more, it’s not worth the asking price simply because it’s not scary. Which is a shame considering it’s all the work of a solo developer, but there’s very little redeeming about it. Stupid Never Dies Stupid Never Dies concept of a post-apocalyptic world with a supernatural pecking order, where the protagonist, an undead named Davy, lies at the bottom, is intriguing. Alas, the actual plot is something far less interesting and surprisingly creepy. The core gameplay loop involves mindless runs through a roguelike dungeon, and while the art style evokes a bit of Suda51, it does very little to capture that inherent charm and campiness.
